title: Caller-Driven Types vs impl Trait
goal: Allow callers to choose the target type using turbofish syntax.
hints: Look at who decides the concrete type: generic T lets the caller choose, while impl Trait lets the function choose.
Turbofish requires an explicit generic parameter T on the function signature.
explanation: Declaring `<T: FromStr>(s: &str) -> T` defines a function where the caller chooses `T` via turbofish syntax `convert::<i32>`. Returning `impl FromStr` means the function itself fixes the return type, making turbofish explicit arguments invalid (`E0632`). Omitting the `FromStr` bound on `T` causes `s.parse()` to fail with `E0277` because parsing requires `FromStr`. Passing `impl FromStr` into turbofish syntax produces error `E0782`.
